title: Store depot event times as the moments they name

blocks.text: A parcel service takes delivery events from partner depots around the world and stores each one as an `Instant`. Each depot sends its local time with its offset from UTC, in the ISO form:

These three are the same moment. When a support agent opens a parcel's page, its history shows each event as the agent's own clock read it, like `2031-11-14 15:00` for an agent in Asia/Kolkata. The service runs on servers set to UTC; its agents are not.

items: `receivedAt(...)`: the moment a depot's event time names;
`forAgent(...)`: that moment as the agent's clock showed it, to the minute.

cases.says: an event time with offset +00:00 is read as that moment
an agent on UTC sees the event's date and time to the minute
an event time with a non-zero offset is read as the moment it names, not as UTC
an event time that writes UTC as Z is read
the history shows the agent's own clock, not the server's

origin.section: An Offset in the Text Is Part of the Value, So Parse Into a Type That Keeps It

concepts: A pattern formatter prints an Instant only after withZone gives it a zone.
Text with an offset is parsed into OffsetDateTime, ZonedDateTime or Instant; LocalDateTime drops the offset silently, and a pattern with xxx refuses Z.
